newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Transavia seeks to avoid multi-million loss.
newsitem.headline: Transavia seeks to avoid multi-million loss.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV's charter subsidiary Transavia said on Wednesday it was planning cost cuts to avoid multi-million guilder losses in the 1996/97 fiscal year.
"We are facing losses of several million guilders unless action is taken," Transavia spokesman Han Tonnen said.
He said the airline's chief executive officer Pieter Legro asked staff to suggest ways of cutting costs and boosting revenues.
Transavia also employed an external consultancy to review performance on some routes, Tonnen said. It was too early to say whether any routes would be dropped.
Transavia, 80 percent-owned by KLM, has been badly hit by a severe downturn in holiday bookings, increased airline competition and rising fuel prices.
"Because holidays are our core business we are more exposed to the vagaries of the airline market than others," Tonnen said.
Transavia's operating profit plunged 71 percent to 4.52 million guilders in the 1995/96 year ended March 31.
